name: Cheese Souffle
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Melt butter in a saucepan; mix smoothly with it flour, salt and cayenne and milk; simmer the mixture gently over the fire, stirring it all the time, till it is as thick as melted butter.
Turn it into a basin, and mix with it the yolks of two well-beaten eggs.
Whisk three whites to a solid froth, and just before the souffle is baked put them into it, and pour the mixture into a small round tin.
It should be only half filled, as the fondu will rise very high.
Pin a napkin around the dish in which it is baked, and serve the moment it is baked.
Have a metal cover strongly heated.
Bake twenty minutes. Sufficient for six persons.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Melt butter in a saucepan; mix smoothly with it flour, salt and cayenne and milk; simmer the mixture gently over the fire, stirring it all the time, till it is as thick as melted butter.
2. Stir into it finely-grated cheese.
3. Turn it into a basin, and mix with it the yolks of two well-beaten eggs.
4. Whisk three whites to a solid froth, and just before the souffle is baked put them into it, and pour the mixture into a small round tin.
5. It should be only half filled, as the fondu will rise very high.
6. Pin a napkin around the dish in which it is baked, and serve the moment it is baked.
7. Have a metal cover strongly heated.
8. Bake twenty minutes. Sufficient for six persons.
